HP:0000588.label: Optic disc coloboma
HP:0000588.text: coloboma of the optic nerve head

records.label: Original family
quotes: A new syndrome characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis has been described.
The family history suggests either an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linkage.

records.label: Proband (male patient)

phenotypes.text: coloboma of the optic nerve head

quotes: We report on a patient with CHARGE syndrome, as manifested by a coloboma of the optic nerve head, congenital heart defect (ASD, VSD, and parachute mitral valve), choanal atresia, severe growth retardation, genital hypoplasia, abnormal ears, cleft lip and palate, and pectus carinatum.
His chromosomes were normal. He died at 19 months.

records.label: Mother of proband
quotes: His mother was short and had hearing impairment, choanal atresia, and a coloboma.

records.label: Previously reported family with new X-linked syndrome
quotes: Previously, we reported on a family with a new syndrome of cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis.
Re-evaluation of new X-linked syndrome for evidence of CHARGE syndrome or association.

records.label: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome family
records.segregation: tracked with the phenotype in this family
quotes: This study hypothesized a possible involvement of TBX22 in a family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, of unknown etiology.
The phenotype extends to additional features including sensorineural deafness and coloboma
A novel TBX22 splice acceptor mutation (c.593-5T>A) was identified that tracked with the phenotype in this family.

notes.statement: Pauws et al. (2013) found a novel TBX22 splice donor variant (c.767+5G>A) and a known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G>A), affecting the same exon as the Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome mutation, in patients with classic X-linked cleft palate phenotypes.
quotes: A novel splice donor variant (c.767+5G>A) and a known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G>A) affecting the same exon were identified in patients with classic CPX phenotypes

notes.statement: Pauws et al. (2013) used in silico and in vitro splicing studies and predicted that all 3 variants abolished normal mRNA splicing; an in vitro assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome. They concluded that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, which expands the phenotypic spectrum of TBX22 mutations.
quotes: All three variants were predicted to abolish normal mRNA splicing and an in vitro assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome.
most importantly confirms that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, expanding the phenotypic spectrum of TBX22 mutations.

notes.statement: Pauws et al. (2013) noted that the developmental expression pattern of Tbx22 suggests the additional features of sensorineural deafness and coloboma seen in Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, although these features had not previously been associated with X-linked cleft palate.
quotes: The phenotype extends to additional features including sensorineural deafness and coloboma, which are suggested by the Tbx22 developmental expression pattern but not previously associated in CPX patients.

notes.statement: Davenport et al. (1986) described the external ear anomalies of CHARGE syndrome: short, wide pinnae that were often cupped and asymmetric, a distinctive triangular concha, a break between the antihelix and antitragus, and 'snipped-off' portions of the helical folds. They stated that the ear pattern was so distinctive that a preliminary diagnosis of CHARGE syndrome could often be made from ear shape alone.
quotes: This paper describes the external ear anomalies found in this syndrome: short wide pinnae, often cupped and asymmetrical; distinctive triangular concha; discontinuity between the antihelix and antitragus; and 'snipped-off' portions of the helical folds.
The patterns of anomalies are so distinctive that a preliminary diagnosis of CHARGE Syndrome can often be made on the basis of ear shape alone.

notes.statement: Metlay et al. (1987) reported a boy with CHARGE syndrome whose mother was short and had hearing impairment, choanal atresia, and coloboma. They suggested that this was evidence for dominant transmission of the disorder in this family.
quotes: His mother was short and had hearing impairment, choanal atresia, and a coloboma. We suggest that this represents evidence for dominant transmission of this disorder in this family.

notes.statement: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) did a follow-up study of the family they had reported earlier with cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis. This family had been cited as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome, but the authors concluded that the patients did not have familial CHARGE syndrome.
quotes: This family has been cited in several reports as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome.
We conclude that our patients do not have familial CHARGE syndrome.

notes.statement: Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) concluded that the family history suggested either autosomal dominant inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linked inheritance.
quotes: The family history suggests either an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linkage.
